section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "He commanded salvations for Yaakov" refers to drawing down the 370 lights of Arich Anpin, which are needed specifically for Yaakov's descent to Charan.
section.t: And it can be said that this is what is brought in Torah Ohr and Torah Chayim immediately following "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva" — the verse:
"He commanded salvations for Yaakov,"
which is the drawing down of the aspect of the 370 lights of Arich Anpin.
For just as the concept of salvation in its simple sense is assistance and the granting of a special power not in the usual manner,
and this granting of power is specifically for the person being saved, who is in a most lowly state and in need of salvation,
so too is it in the inner interpretation of "salvations,"
that their essence is the 370 lights of Arich Anpin,
whose drawing down
(to Yaakov)
is specifically for the state of his going out from Be'er Sheva and his journey to Charan.
For in order that he be able to draw down the yud even in Charan,
there must be "He commanded salvations for Yaakov,"
to draw down to Yaakov the 370 lights of Arich Anpin, which are above the chain of descent,
above even the yud of the Name Havayah,
the yud of Yaakov.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the word "commanded" implies connection and union, so that the 370 lights, though higher than Yaakov, become united with him internally, ensuring his prayer's fulfillment.
section.t: And one should add precision to the wording of the verse, "He commanded salvations for Yaakov"
(specifically "commanded"),
that the drawing down of the salvations
(the 370 lights)
to Yaakov shall be in a manner of "command,"
a term of connection and union.
For although the 370 lights are above Yaakov,
above even the yud within him,
nevertheless,
they will be connected and united with him,
so that they are given over to him internally.
And through the drawing down to Yaakov of the aforementioned aspect of salvations
(for the sake of his journey to Charan),
he was certain
(even before his journey to Charan)
that his prayer would be fulfilled,
that "He will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear,"
and beyond that — "and I will return in peace to my father's house,"
and beyond that — "and Havayah will be my G-d,"
and beyond that — "and this stone which I have set as a pillar will be a house of G-d."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yaakov took multiple stones of the place and made them into one stone at his head, elevating it above his own head (the yud), and prayed that this stone become a house for G-d's very Essence.
section.t: Now, Yaakov's prayer
(in the manner of a vow)
"If G-d will be with me... and this stone... will be a house of G-d" came after the act of "he took
from the stones of the place and placed them at his headrest."
And the explanation is:
"Place" is the definition of "world,"
as it is brought in Tanya
that the definition of the world is "place"
(and time).
[And although "Place" is a name of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called "Place,"
because He is the Place of the world,
nevertheless, this matter is in concealment,
and what is felt in revelation in the place is the world.
For this is that Havayah squared numerically equals "place,"
meaning that the essence of Havayah drawn into place is only in a manner of gematria, which is the numerical value of the letters,
for the numerical value indicates
a diminution of light, etc., diminution after diminution].
And "the stones of the place"
(the aspect of the inanimate)
are the lowest type in the world.
And within this itself, "stones" in the plural,
as they are in a state of multiplicity and division.
And this is "he took from the stones of the place and placed them at his headrest,"
that Yaakov made
from the stones of the place
(stones in the plural)
one stone
[therefore it is written "and he placed" and not "and he placed them"],
and moreover,
"and he placed them at his headrest,"
that he raised and elevated the stone until it was level with his head,
and it can be said even more, that the stone was above his head
of Yaakov,
meaning above the aspect of the yud of Yaakov
(which is his head,
as above).
And upon this he prayed, "and this stone... will be a house of G-d,"
that this stone
(one stone,
which he made from a multiplicity of stones)
will be not only above the aspect of the head
(the yud)
of Yaakov,
but will be even higher — a house of G-d,
a house
(and dwelling place)
for His very Essence.
